newsitem.title: FRANCE: Daewoo questions French Thomson move.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo questions French Thomson move.

text.p: Daewoo Electronics chairman Soon Hoon Bae said he did not understand France's decision to suspend a planned sale of Thomson SA and said Daewoo was still interested in acquiring Thomson Multimedia.
He criticised the basis for the privatisation commission's decision and said the publicity around the decision had hurt Daewoo's reputation.
He also attacked the lack of decision in the French government.
"It's all confused," Bae told financial daily Les Echos.

"Yesterday I was in industry minister Franck Borotra's office. He could not explain to me why the commission refused our offer, nor what was going to happen in the future. How can I invest in a country if I dont understand the path of political decision," he said.
Les Echos reported that Bae said Daewoo's French investment policy was separate from the Thomson affair.

France's independent privatisation commission rejected the state's plan to sell Thomson to Lagardere because Lagardere was going to sell consumer electronics unit Thomson Multimedia to Daewoo. The commission said the sale would have transferred valuable French technology to Korea.
It also said that Daewoo's promise to create 5,000 jobs in France if it won Thomson Multimedia had no guarantees and so could not be enforced.
Bae rejected these as unfounded criticisms.
"With regard to digital technology, the real added value is in Thomson Broadcast Systems which would have been part of a 50-50 joint venture with Lagardere," Bae said.

"As far as digital televisions are concerned, we are ahead since we just commercialised in the United States our first television linked to the internet. And as for liquid crystal technologies (for flat screens), it is lodged in Sextant which will remain part of Thomson-CSF."
Bae said the decoder technology which now belongs to Thomson was developed in the United States and owed very little to French state involvement.

Bae also noted that when Lagardere first came up with the plan, it wrote to Thomson Chairman Marcel Roulet to find out whether Daewoo's involvement would pose a problem. Roulet answered that it would not.
Bae said that the commission's attack on Daewoo's investment and job creation plan was unfair since the government had never asked him for any guarantees.
"I never had to explain myself. If the state wanted guarantees, we could have thought about it," he said.
"Apart from Thomson, there's no major player in the sector in France but we have since received a few proposals in specific areas," he said.
"If there's a decision to separate Thomson-CSF, it will take six months, and TMM (Thomson Multimedia) is losing money daily."
Les Echos said that Bae had hinted that its offer would have to be a lower sum given the latest delays and the company's problems.
